high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Late Uruk cylinder-seal illustration: a granary keeper retains one clay receipt with a distinctive ibex impression after issuing one grain measure, then compares a retried request made with the same cylinder and leaves every second measure untouched, in one secular clay frieze without cuneiform, labels or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A full ochre clay field is divided by two shallow horizontal ground grooves and enclosed by one plain rolled border, with every form rendered as flat black incision and muted terracotta infill. The composition contains no modeled depth, photographic light, gradient, cuneiform wedge, alphabet, numeral, caption, arrow, flowchart, deity, temple ritual, ruler, throne, weapon, national emblem, coin, magical seal or modern machine.

elements.desc: Flat-fronted granary structure occupying the right half, built from reed bundles and mud-brick rectangles with one open storage bay and a low issuing ledge. A row of untouched grain measures remains visible inside after one measure has left; the structure has no inscription, tally marks, cuneiform, number, signboard, throne, guarded cage, directional marker or mechanical dispenser.

Adult Late Uruk granary keeper standing at center, medium-brown skin, shoulder-length black hair, plain ankle-length cream wool skirt and bare feet. In calm side profile, he holds a retained clay bulla near a fresh impression for direct comparison while his other hand rests away from the stored measures; he wears no crown, badge, weapon, divine horns or authority staff.

Late Uruk requester standing at left, dark-brown skin, short curly black hair, terracotta wool skirt and bare feet. With a neutral expression, both hands roll one dark stone cylinder across a fresh clay lump on a reed mat, reproducing the request after interruption; he carries no grain measure, coin, written tablet, crown, weapon, divine attribute or command gesture.

Late Uruk recipient walking toward lower-left, medium-brown skin, straight black hair tied low, muted-red wool skirt and bare feet. He carries exactly one filled reed grain measure against his torso, the completed issue, while remaining equal in scale to the requester and keeper; no second measure, payment, medal, badge, royal garment or victory gesture appears.

Retained oval clay receipt resting in the keeper's left palm, impressed with one original secular ibex beside a three-petal plant and pierced once for storage. The motif is crisp enough to match the fresh request but functions only as identity evidence; it contains no cuneiform, alphabet, numeral, royal portrait, deity, magical claim, official state crest or written verdict.

Fresh clay request on the reed mat before the requester, carrying the identical ibex-and-three-petal impression produced by the nearby dark stone cylinder. Its size, orientation and every incised feature match the retained receipt, making the repeated identity visible without writing; it bears no number, caption, approval mark, arrow, divine sign, coin image or alternate motif.

Group of untouched empty reed grain measures aligned inside the granary bay, all equal in size with open tops and plain dark rims. None has crossed the issuing ledge during the repeated request, while the recipient's single filled measure remains outside; the group carries no numbering, label, lock, warning sign, status light, arrow, ownership crest or ranking order.

Small dark stone cylinder seal lying beside the fresh clay, carved in reverse with the same secular ibex and three-petal plant found on both impressions. Its drilled center and rolled form remain visible, identifying the stable request source without becoming a symbol of truth or sovereignty; it has no inscription, cuneiform, crown, deity, weapon or modern key shape.
